title: Why site engineers wait three weeks for a reimbursement
summary: Claims in your real estate expense reimbursement process can take over three weeks to settle. See where time goes, its impact, and how to speed things up.
body_markdown:
Devon, a site engineer, has two options when his facility's chiller dies. Wait weeks for a purchase order while the building slow-cooks in the October heat, or shell out AED 640 trusting the expense reimbursement process.


Devon has a soft spot for a working air conditioner, so he pays the bill and saves the day. Three weeks later, his employee reimbursement request still says "under review."


That's the everyday reality of expense reimbursement in real estate.


While the claim process is usually simple, delays build in the handoffs after submission. With approvers on site, receipts in pockets, and weekly payment runs, nobody has added up the waiting.


Smooth[spend management for real estate groups](https://www.alaan.com/industries/real-estate) hinges on knowing the queue is building and cutting the idle days between steps. This blog covers what each stage of a claim costs you in days, how to shorten the slowest ones, and the VAT and legal points to keep in mind.


## Where does the time go in an expense reimbursement claim?


Waiting on a claim is five shorter ones stacked end to end, each perfectly reasonable on its own. Nobody in the chain is doing anything wrong, which is exactly why nobody has added it up.


Let's see where time usually flies as the claim follows the typical reimbursement process.


### 1. Receipt travels in your pocket: 2 days


After making the fix, the most natural next step is to slip the receipt into your pocket. By the time you're back at a laptop, the receipt has visited two sites and maybe nearly a washing machine.


The claim hasn't been filed yet, but it's been at least two days since the payment.


**Where all receipts end up!** Fuel, parking, and toll top-ups all follow, almost like fate. A[mileage reimbursement policy](https://www.alaan.com/blog/employee-mileage-fuel-reimbursement-policies) or clear per-diem rules settle what counts before the claim, so nobody is digging through the laundry later.


### 2. Reimbursement claim is submitted once a month: At least 6 days


Out-of-pocket expenses happen often in real estate. After finding the receipt, site staff submits a batch of claims once a fortnight or month. Depending on when the purchase landed, that wait can run from a few days to nearly a month.


This is the longest single wait in the chain. While nobody caused it, batch submissions may point to a payout frequency issue.


### 3. Claims queue for an approver: 4 days


When the batch finally goes in, it lands with a site manager who spends the day under equipment, not at a desk. Approvals happen in the gaps between jobs, usually on a phone with a signal that comes and goes.


A claim that arrives in a busy week can sit for days. The manager isn't ignoring it, just fixing something else first.


### 4. Finance queries missing details: 5 days


An approved claim reaches finance in hopes of settlement. But sometimes the supplier forgets to add their TRN on the invoice, or the amount doesn't match the card slip. Each gap is small, but each one stops the claim.


A query goes out, gets read a bit late, then corrected a little later. Every round of that takes days.


### 5. Claim waits for the next payment run: 4 days


Finally, the paperwork is fixed, the claim is approved, and finance teams are content. All that's left is the automated payment cycle. Whether that's once a week or month, the claim waits for the next one.


Three weeks is usually the light side of the wait. Real queues run longer with overdue claims, public holidays like Eid, approvers on leave, and suppliers who take a week to reissue an invoice.


## What does a slow reimbursement cost the business?


Slow reimbursement creates issues in accounting, staff morale, and even service quality. Let's go through each impact.


### Staff stop spending on what the job needs


Fronting money for a replacement once is generosity; twice is a hobby. When reimbursements slow down, urgent parts will wait for a purchase order. Soon enough, the cost turns up as downtime instead of a claim.


Nobody records that as a reimbursement problem, so nobody connects the two.


### Late claims land in the wrong period


When a claim queues or is queried for a long time, it can slip into the next VAT period. With cost showing up in the wrong month's books, you lose track of actual spend, and the input VAT lands on a return it doesn't belong to.


The FTA also allows[two tax periods to recover input VAT](https://www.tax.gov.ae/-/media/Files/FTA/links/Public-Clarification/Time-frame-for-recovering-Input-Tax.pdf) . If you miss both, you've got to file a voluntary disclosure and extra paperwork.


### Finance spends its time chasing


Every email, reminder, and request for invoice corrections pulls finance off reconciliations and month-end close. Across every claim in the queue makes chasing a part-time job nobody was hired for.


One major[disadvantage of reimbursement](https://www.alaan.com/blog/employee-expense-reimbursements-disadvantages) is that when the claim becomes urgent, other operations take a toll, too.


## How does expense reimbursement in real estate work?


In the UAE’s commercial real estate landscape, expense reimbursements are a routine yet often frustrating part of lease management. Landlords or property managers incur shared operational expenses, such as utilities, maintenance, or security, and recover them from tenants based on what’s outlined in their lease agreements.


While the concept is simple, the execution is where things frequently break down, especially when multiple properties, tenants, and vendors are involved.


### Lease clauses set the ground rules


Reimbursement obligations are typically defined in lease clauses, particularly in net lease structures (e.g., triple net or modified gross leases). These specify:


- Which expenses are recoverable (e.g., common area maintenance, utilities, insurance)
- How tenant shares are calculated (usually pro-rata based on floor area)
- Billing and payment timelines
- Caps, exclusions, and audit rights


In the UAE, service charge transparency is increasingly regulated, especially in freehold areas governed by **RERA** (Dubai) or **DMT** (Abu Dhabi), making clean documentation not just a best practice but a compliance requirement.


### Reimbursement calculations and allocation


Expenses are typically allocated based on a tenant’s pro-rata share of the total rentable area.


***Pro Rata Share = Tenant's Rentable Square Footage ÷ Building's Total Rentable Square Footage***


**For example:**


- Building size: 50,000 square feet
- Tenant space: 5,000 square feet
- Pro rata share: 10%
- If total building CAM expenses are AED 100,000, this tenant pays AED 10,000


Some leases use variations of this formula, such as adjusting for occupancy rates or applying different calculations for specific expense categories.


### Reimbursement process


The typical reimbursement process follows these steps:


1. **Expense tracking** : The landlord records all reimbursable expenses throughout the year
2. **Allocation** : Expenses are allocated to tenants based on lease terms
3. **Estimating** : Annual estimates are divided into monthly or quarterly payments
4. **Billing** : Tenants receive regular statements for their share
5. **Reconciliation** : At year-end, actual expenses are compared with estimates, resulting in credits or additional charges
6. **Payment** : Tenants pay according to the terms in their lease


The reconciliation process is particularly important, as it ensures accurate accounting for all parties. If estimated payments were higher than actual expenses, tenants receive credits; if lower, they must pay the difference.


Efficient processing requires organised record-keeping and clear communication. This process becomes time-consuming when:


- Expense records are spread across teams or spreadsheets
- Receipts are missing or incorrectly tagged
- Tenant billing doesn’t match what’s recoverable under the lease
- [VAT](https://www.alaan.com/blog/vat-registration-uae) treatment is misclassified, leading to reporting risk


Manual systems are rarely audit-ready, and reconciling late or incorrectly increases friction with tenants, damages trust, and impacts cash flow.


Hence, Many property managers now use specialised software to track expenses and generate accurate billing statements.

## What VAT evidence do you need for site expenses?


Reimbursing an employee does not automatically make the VAT recoverable. For site spend, finance needs the right evidence to support the input VAT claim and show that the purchase meets the FTA's recovery conditions.


**Documents needed for reimbursed site expenses:**


- **A valid tax invoice** showing the supplier, goods or services supplied, and VAT charged.
- **Details of the purchase** showing what was bought and how it relates to the business.
- **The VAT amount charged** so finance can identify the input VAT being claimed.
- **The reimbursement claim** linking the purchase to the employee who incurred the expense.
- **Supporting payment records** that help finance match the claim, transaction, and invoice.


A clear[expense reimbursement policy](https://www.alaan.com/blog/employee-expense-reimbursement-taxable-implications) should make these checks part of the claim process, rather than leaving them until the VAT return.[Corporate cards](https://www.alaan.com/products/corporate-cards) can also capture transaction data and receipts closer to the point of spend.


Getting the evidence right at the point of spend gives finance what it needs to assess VAT recovery before the claim is settled.


## Legal considerations for site reimbursement in the UAE


The UAE Labour Law ([Federal Decree-Law 33 of 2021](https://uaelegislation.gov.ae/en/legislations/1541) ) doesn't set a deadline for paying staff back, so your contract and expense policy carry that weight. Where a policy goes further than the law, the more favourable term applies (Article 65), so write down only what you can keep to.


Three rules shape how you handle claims day to day. Each is easy to overlook until a claim is rejected, late, or still open when someone resigns.


**Labour law highlights for your policy:**


- **Deductions.** If a claim is paid and later rejected, you can't deduct it from salary. Article 25 allows only specific deductions, and overpayment recovery is capped at 20% of the wage.
- **Leavers.** Final dues are payable within 14 days of the contract ending (Article 53), so clear any open claims before the last day.
- **Records.** Keep invoices and approvals for five years for VAT and seven for corporate tax, since that's the retention period the FTA expects.


This is general guidance, so have your legal team check the policy wording before it goes live. Doing it before the first dispute is cheaper than rewriting a policy mid-claim.


## How to speed up the expense reimbursement process


Speeding up expense reimbursement starts with removing the queues between spending, approval, and payment. For site teams, that means changing how expenses are approved, captured, and paid, and reducing the number of manual handoffs.


All that needs is the right mix of[expense management](https://www.alaan.com/products/expense-management) workflows, schedules, and payment tools.


### Approve expenses before the money moves


Set approval rules before employees spend, with limits based on the purchase type, amount, or site. This moves the approval decision to the start of the process and removes the wait for managers to review a claim.


Intelligent workflows can route claims to the right approver, and[accounting automation](https://www.alaan.com/products/accounting-automation) reduces manual records and reconciliation. Task execution may slow down at the start, but never as much as a new PO.


### Capture receipts at the point of spend


Let employees record receipts immediately after an expense. Closing the gap between the transaction and its documentation avoids missing receipts and keeps them legible. A mobile device is usually enough to upload receipts as documents in real time.


[Artificial intelligence in finance](https://www.alaan.com/blog/need-artificial-intelligence-ai) is the right place to look for automated transaction mapping through card swipes and receipt photos. Alaan's[OpenAI integration](https://www.alaan.com/blog/announcing-our-integration-with-openai) also classifies and processes expense data down to employee ID, project, property, or expense category.


### Run payments more often


Move your reimbursement runs to a schedule that matches your claims request volume. Going from monthly to weekly makes a huge difference. With shorter payment runs, claims don't sit unprocessed because they missed the payment cycle.


While[AI is reshaping finance](https://www.alaan.com/blog/the-future-of-ai-in-finance-how-is-ai-reshaping-the-financial-landscape) , more frequent payment runs can add automation overhead. Combine reimbursements with existing high-frequency workflows (like petty cash top-ups) instead of monthly salary credits or vendor payments.


### Give site staff company cards


Real estate is constantly full of supplies, equipment, transport, or other site expenses. Using[employee expense cards](https://www.alaan.com/services/employee-expense-cards) and corporate cards to handle categorised transactions ends the constant chase for reimbursement.


Corporate cards also add spend control and reduce out-of-pocket spending. Company cards can have employee-, category-, and even merchant-level limits, so finance can control where company money goes without slowing down site teams.


To fix the whole financial workflow and set a baseline, you should map your spend to the settlement process ahead of time. ## Frequently asked questions


### How long should expense reimbursement take?


Any business's expense reimbursement process should take a few days. Once an employee submits a complete claim, it should move through approval and settlement without queuing. In real estate companies, many manual handoffs and wait times stretch this beyond three weeks.


### Are employers required to reimburse business expenses?


UAE labour law does not explicitly mention an employer's duty to cover business expenses. These obligations are usually set out in legally binding work contracts. To avoid disputes, employers should clearly define eligible expenses, required documentation, and payment processes.


### What documentation is required for expense reimbursement?


Employees should provide the receipt or tax invoice, details of the purchase, and enough information to show why it was a business expense. For VAT recovery, finance teams also need the evidence required under the FTA's input VAT rules.


### How can you reimburse site staff faster?


Start by capturing receipts at the point of spend and approving expenses before payment. Weekly payment runs can cut waiting time, while company cards can remove the reimbursement step for regular site purchases altogether.
